title: 1971 AHSME Problem 34
statement: An ordinary clock in a factory is running slow so that the minute hand passes the hour hand at the usual dial positions (\(12\) o’clock, etc.) but only every \(69\) minutes. At time and one-half for overtime, the extra pay to which a \(\$4.00\)-per-hour worker should be entitled after working a normal \(8\)-hour day by that slow-running clock is:

solutions.text:
Successive hand-overlaps are \(\frac{720}{11}\) real minutes apart, while this slow clock displays \(69\) minutes between them. Thus \(12\) displayed hours correspond to \(759\) real minutes, since \[ 11\cdot69=759=12\cdot60+39. \] Eight displayed hours therefore take \(8\) hours \(26\) minutes, so the overtime is \(26\) minutes. At \(\$6\) per hour, that pays \(\$2.60.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: A normal clock’s hands pass every \(\frac{720}{11}\) minutes
Eleven slow-clock intervals total \(12\) displayed hours but \(12\) hours \(39\) minutes of real time
